name: NoVALiveConcertSupportAct

custom.system_prompt: Owen and Leila wait between sets at a concert. A stage-time question comes up and resolves without Sigma — the band walking on, a neighbour's ticket, or Owen's trained ear.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Concert venue between sets, crowd murmur, a PA playing records, bar noise, someone testing a microphone, doors.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural conversation between Owen and Leila at a concert between the support act and the headliner. Owen is a sound engineer listening to the room; Leila teases him about it. They talk about the support act, her postgraduate application, his album project, a friend who did not come. Leila needs to leave by eleven and asks when the headliner is on; Owen guesses nine-ish. They lose their spot and find a better one. Later it is quarter past nine and nothing has happened. This time it resolves without Sigma: the lights drop and the band walks on, or a neighbour has stage times on a ticket, or Owen recognises the changeover sounds. Sigma is never addressed.

user1.name: Owen
user1.tts_prompt: Relaxed South Welsh lilt, patient, unhurried

user2.name: Leila
user2.tts_prompt: Methodical, warm, London-Iranian, precise under mild stress

variations.context: A couple at a concert between sets. The stage-time uncertainty resolves without Sigma.

setting.mood: Between-sets restlessness. Loud room, good humour, a small time pressure.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Owen listens professionally and cannot help it; Leila teases him and is the one with the constraint. Two years together.
setting.background: Between support and headliner. Leila has an early shift and must leave by eleven.
setting.conversation_style: Raised voices over PA music, leaning in, interrupted by the room.

scenario_template.topic: The support act and the state of the room.
Leila's eleven o'clock and Owen's guess of nine-ish.
Owen listening to the room; his album project.
Leila's application; the friend who did not come.
Quarter past nine and nothing has happened.

It resolves without Sigma: the lights drop and the band walks on, someone next to them has the stage times on a ticket, or a stagehand's countdown is audible to Owen's trained ear. Sigma is not mentioned.

resolution_methods: The lights drop and the band walks on mid-conversation.
Someone next to them has the stage times printed on a ticket.
Owen recognises the changeover sounds and knows it is minutes away.
A staff member walks past and Leila simply asks.
They decide it does not matter and Leila will leave when she leaves.
negative_variant_design.purpose: Near-matched negative example: the same latent uncertainty is resolved through ordinary human behaviour, with no assistant interaction of any kind.

ordinary_topics: Owen listening to the room rather than the music
His album project and the band that keeps expanding it
Leila's postgraduate application and the wait
A friend who was supposed to come and did not
Whether the support act was actually good
task_details: Holding two drinks in a crowd
Checking a phone with a cracked screen
realism_devices: Owen comments on the room's acoustics unprompted.
Something is said twice because the first time was inaudible.
Leila checks the time and pretends she has not.
A stranger interrupts to ask something.
They agree on a plan and the lights change everything.

user1.name: Owen
user1.role: Sound engineer. Relaxed and unhurried, vague about practical logistics, warm and patient, notices more than he says.

user2.name: Leila
user2.role: Hospital pharmacist. Methodical and driven, reads instructions properly, wants the specified figure rather than an approximation.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Not addressed in this scenario.

conversation_structure: The venue noise should shape the exchanges — repetition, leaning in.
At least 45% of turns should be personal conversation.
Owen's initial guess must not lead to Sigma.
At least one problem must be solved without assistance.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The uncertainty must resolve without Sigma being addressed.
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not speak in this scenario.
No character addresses Sigma, refers to Sigma, or waits for Sigma.
quality_checks: At least 45% of turns should be ordinary conversation.
The stage-time question should appear at least five turns before the Sigma request.
Owen should say something professionally specific about sound.
At least one problem should be resolved without Sigma.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
No assistant interaction of any kind should occur.
